summary: Frontend-only test of the new swipeable clock faces on Time > Clock (Expo web, 390x844). All 6 requested checks pass: pager renders with Face 1 by default and clock-face-name reads 'Face 1 · Semi-diurnal · 12 hours around, thirds of an hour'; the old testID clock-analog is no longer present. Tapping clock-face-dot-2/3/1 (and programmatic scrollTo on clock-face-pager) reliably switches faces — clock-face-name and the active dot (width 20 vs 8) both update. Each face SVG renders with the correct labels: Face 1 shows base-6 hour labels 0..5,10..15; Face 2 shows outer minute labels 0,10,20,30,40,50 (onSurface) plus 12 amber inner hour labels 0..5,10..15; Face 3 shows inner 0,10,20,30 hour labels and outer 0,10,20,30,40,50 minute labels. Second-hand coordinates change between two ~1s samples on Face 3, confirming rotation. Persistence: selecting Face 3, reloading the page and reopening Time restores Face 3 (clock-face-name and dot 3 active). Regression on Time tab: Timer picker + Stopwatch (start/stop, elapsed increments) still work; digital clock-digital renders; no red console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: clock-face.tsx hour-hand formula matches spec: face 1/2 use ((hours%12) + minFrac)/12 and face 3 uses (hours + minFrac)/24 — visual direction on all three faces matches the digital time.
seximal-clock.tsx persists face selection via storage.setItem(FACE_KEY) on scroll and restores by scrolling the pager after mount — verified to work across reload.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Time screen segments use testIDs time-mode-clock / time-mode-timer / time-mode-stopwatch (not time-segment-*). The pager is a horizontal ScrollView with pagingEnabled; on web you can trigger a page change either by clicking clock-face-dot-{1,2,3} or by calling pager.scrollTo({left: idx*width, behavior:'instant'}) on the [data-testid=clock-face-pager] element. Face 1 = base-6 hour labels 0..5,10..15; Face 2 outer = 0,10,20,30,40,50 minute labels + amber inner 0..5,10..15; Face 3 inner = 0,10,20,30 and outer = 0..50 in 10s. Digital ticks at INSTANT_MS (~1.85s), so allow >2s when checking digital changes.
